guidance: Format codes follow the C and POSIX strftime conventions with English names. This page does not look up IANA zones or daylight-saving rules, so enter the offset in force at the instant you are formatting; %Z prints that offset (UTC or UTC+05:30), not a zone abbreviation.
method: strftime format codes are expanded against the Unix instant shifted by the chosen UTC offset. The offset is parsed as +HH:MM or +HHMM (a leading minus is accepted) and limited to -12:00 through +14:00. The instant stays the input epoch: %s returns it unchanged rather than re-deriving it from the shifted wall clock. Calendar fields come from the shifted time read in UTC, so no device time zone or daylight-saving rule is consulted; the page formats the wall clock the entered offset describes. %j is the one-based day of the year. %U counts weeks from the first Sunday and %W from the first Monday, and both leave the days before it in week 00. %V is the ISO 8601 week number and %G its week-based year, which belongs to the year that owns the week's Thursday, so 2021-01-01 is 2020-W53. %u numbers Monday 1 to Sunday 7 and %w numbers Sunday 0 to Saturday 6. %I and %l map midnight and noon to 12. %C truncates the year to its century, and %y and %g keep the last two digits. The GNU flags - (no padding), _ (space padding) and 0 (zero padding) apply to the fixed-width numeric fields; %e, %k and %l are space-padded by default and the other fixed-width numbers are zero-padded. Weekday and month names are English, and the locale composites %c, %x, %X and %D use the English C-locale forms, so the result does not depend on the browser locale. %Z is the offset label (UTC or UTC+HH:MM), not an IANA abbreviation. Unknown codes and a trailing % are copied through unchanged and reported. The format is limited to 240 characters and the Unix time to 0001-01-01 through 9999-12-31. Everything is computed in the browser; nothing is stored or fetched.
